macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall as tech earnings revive AI-spending concerns
items.summary: The Dow fell 0.3%, the S&P 500 declined 0.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 1.4% in Thursday trading. Alphabet’s results renewed concerns over whether massive artificial-intelligence investments will generate sufficient returns.[3][7][10]

items.title: Fed holds rates steady but officials signal possible December tightening
items.summary: The Federal Reserve voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark rate in the 3.75%–4.00% range. Markets continued to price in a meaningful probability of a 25-basis-point December hike, while St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said additional tightening may soon be necessary.[2][4][5]

items.title: U.S. GDP beats expectations while inflation remains elevated
items.summary: Third-quarter U.S. GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate, exceeding the 3.2% expectation. Persistent inflation and higher energy costs complicated the outlook after the Fed’s decision to pause rate increases.[5][7][10]

items.title: European and Japanese central banks keep rates unchanged
items.summary: The European Central Bank held its benchmark rate steady while leaving open the possibility of a December increase amid energy-driven inflation. The Bank of Japan also maintained its policy rate at 1.25%, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.4%.[3]

items.title: Amazon shares drop after earnings miss and cautious outlook
items.summary: Amazon reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings and revenue, while offering a cautious holiday-quarter sales outlook. AWS growth remained strong at 39.3%, but investors reacted negatively to the results and increased capital-spending plans.[3][5][10]

items.title: Intel plunges after weak forward guidance
items.summary: Intel shares fell nearly 23% in premarket trading after the chipmaker issued a weak outlook, citing softening PC demand. The report added to pressure on technology stocks already weakened by disappointing Alphabet and Amazon news.[5]

items.title: Alphabet results intensify concerns over AI investment returns
items.summary: Alphabet shares fell sharply after the company reported weaker-than-expected revenue growth, prompting renewed concern about search and advertising trends and the payoff from its large AI infrastructure spending.[5][7][10]

items.title: Microsoft beats estimates while Micron rallies on memory-chip outlook
items.summary: Microsoft shares rose more than 4% in extended trading after beating expectations. Micron gained 5.9% after rival SK Hynix reported quarterly profit growth of more than sevenfold, boosting optimism about memory-chip demand.[1][4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance investigates suspected $6.3 billion security breach
items.summary: Binance is investigating a major exploit reportedly linked to a compromised employee or DevOps laptop. Tether, Circle and other firms have frozen roughly $2.5–$3 billion of assets associated with the incident, while Binance says it will cover user losses.[1][2][3]

items.title: Crypto sell-off triggers more than $1 billion in liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $78,000 amid the Binance incident and broader market weakness. More than $1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated in the past 24 hours, with long positions accounting for most of the losses.[3][6]

items.title: SEC charges firms over alleged $130 million crypto scheme
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission charged two companies accused of defrauding investors through a crypto investment scheme described as resembling a Ponzi structure.[3]

items.title: NYSE owner plans regulated Hyperliquid perpetual-futures market
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange plans to operate a U.S.-regulated, KYC- and AML-compliant perpetual-futures market built on Hyperliquid and has invested in platform partner Trade[.]xyz.[5][6]

items.title: Binance applies for crypto license in Brazil
items.summary: Binance submitted an application for a crypto license in Brazil before the regulatory deadline, beginning a review that does not guarantee approval.[4]

items.title: Ondo Finance launches tokenized portfolios on Solana
items.summary: Ondo Finance introduced seven tokenized investment portfolios on Solana, including products powered by BlackRock and covering income, growth and thematic strategies.[6]

items.title: Chainlink expands 24/7 data for tokenized assets
items.summary: Chainlink launched around-the-clock market data for tokenized stocks and commodities, including reference pricing when traditional markets are closed; Aave is adopting the data for real-world-asset collateral.[5]

items.title: Stellar becomes a default network in MetaMask
items.summary: MetaMask now automatically includes Stellar addresses for eligible accounts, making Stellar a default supported network in the wallet.[6]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for trillion-parameter Large 4
items.summary: Mistral released downloadable weights for Mistral Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model, allowing organizations to run it on their own hardware. The release follows an earlier public preview and reportedly improves coding and cybersecurity performance.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber defense
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on cybersecurity and agentic coding. It reportedly leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is initially being made available to selected cyber defenders rather than the general public.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, a real-time interactive world model that generates steerable environments with native sound, speech and simulated physics. Access is initially limited to trusted testers, with broader availability planned through a waitlist.

items.title: OpenAI reorganizes its Model Spec
items.summary: OpenAI updated its public Model Spec around five core values, adding guidance on context, oversight, human agency and side effects while removing much of its previous detailed style guidance.

items.title: New research targets faster large-language-model inference
items.summary: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton and collaborators introduced FlashMap, a speculative-decoding method that reportedly achieved up to a 6.14-fold lossless speedup on Qwen3-8B by proposing multiple tokens at once.

items.title: Prime Intellect reports faster training with trainable Mega MoE kernel
items.summary: Prime Intellect added a backward pass to DeepSeek’s fused Mega MoE kernel, making it usable for training. The company reports up to 3.11-fold faster mixture-of-experts kernels and as much as 34% higher end-to-end training throughput.

items.title: Microsoft publishes multi-agent coding harness
items.summary: Microsoft researchers open-sourced Agensh, a system that allows up to 1,024 coding agents to divide work among themselves. Initial results suggest that adding agents improves performance, although gains are not linear.

items.title: GitHub expands agent-focused Copilot tools
items.summary: GitHub announced Copilot Fusion and additional agent tools at GitHub Universe 2026. Enterprise customers can also use AI credits rather than traditional Copilot seats, signaling a shift toward usage-based pricing for coding agents.

items.title: Microsoft AI diagnostic system published in Science
items.summary: Microsoft AI’s MAI-DxO diagnostic system was reported to achieve 83% accuracy on difficult NEJM cases, compared with 36% for physicians using books and internet resources in the reported evaluation.

items.title: OpenAI moves frontier-model training offline after internet incident
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly shifted frontier-model training to environments without live internet access after a model reached the internet through a configuration error. Training now uses a cached copy of the web, according to industry coverage.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA reportedly shuts down BioWare and cancels next Mass Effect project
items.summary: Electronic Arts reportedly closed BioWare after cancelling an early Mass Effect project, with the studio’s remaining staff affected by a broader restructuring. Reports link the decision to EA’s leveraged buyout and a shift toward Star Wars development.

items.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders launches on mobile
items.summary: Monster Hunter Outlanders, developed by Tencent’s TiMi Studio Group with Capcom, launched for mobile devices. The game includes adapted controls, shorter play sessions and a new storyline designed for phones.

items.title: Lords of the Fallen II delayed to early 2027
items.summary: CI Games moved Lords of the Fallen II from 2026 to the first quarter of 2027. The title’s closed beta was also postponed to January 2027.

items.title: GameMaker to become free for commercial PC use
items.summary: YoYo Games announced that GameMaker’s next-generation runtime will be free for commercial desktop, mobile and web releases beginning January 1, 2027. Console exports will still require an Enterprise license.

items.title: Ubisoft says no Assassin’s Creed remakes are currently planned
items.summary: Ubisoft said it has no Assassin’s Creed remakes in development following Black Flag Resynced, while confirming continued work on Assassin’s Creed Hexe and multiplayer project Invictus.

items.title: Alien: Isolation 2 details emerge
items.summary: Creative Assembly discussed Alien: Isolation 2 in a 17-minute Q&A, confirming a physical edition and features including a real-world microphone mechanic and photo mode. The sequel is expected in 2027.

items.title: UK games industry calls for expanded government support
items.summary: UKIE urged the British government to modernize the Video Games Expenditure Credit and create new funding programs to help studios address a reported £500,000–£2 million financing gap.

items.title: Pocketpair open to bringing Palworld to Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe said the company would welcome discussions about releasing Palworld on Nintendo’s Switch 2, though no port has been announced.

items.title: Serious Sam: The Third Encounter announced
items.summary: Croteam and Devolver Digital announced Serious Sam: The Third Encounter, a new mainline entry in the shooter series. The game is in early development and currently has a Steam listing.

items.title: Rockstar staff set dates for union-recognition vote
items.summary: Rockstar Games employees are scheduled to vote on union recognition from November 12 to 26, a period that overlaps with the planned launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.
